findings.text: The moved seam-marker assertion reads the whole route source (`source = Path(source_path).read_text(...)`) and asserts each seam marker is present anywhere in the file, where the deleted tests/test_route_default_wiring.py scoped the equivalent assertion to the measure_fixture slice (`fixture_source = oracle_source.split("def measure_fixture",1)[1].split("def _numeric_gate",1)[0]`). Because `_solve_with_defaults(` also names the function definition (scripts/oracle_rebaseline/measure.py:208), the whole-file form is satisfied even if measure_fixture stopped crossing the seam, so this sub-assertion is weaker than the one it replaces. The private-kernel half is stricter (whole-file absence), so the guard is not lost; scoping the marker check back to the fixture would restore the deleted check's strength.

The prescribed-current test asserts target_current passthrough (`oracle_request.target_current == 1.0`) only for the solovev-oracle route; for the topology-visuals route (mast and diiid) it asserts `current` only. The deleted fixture asserted `solve_request.target_current == target_current` for all three routes it exercised, so the target_current passthrough coverage is narrower after the move. Non-blocking: the `current` (prescribed-current vector) passthrough, which the fixture also asserted and which is the defect-prone field, is retained for all three.
